Return to Knysna

By: Catherine Rice | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Knysna, once the jewel of the Garden Route, is on a knife edge - steps to dissolve its council and place the town under administration have been initiated, but is it too little too late?

Unique Selling Point:
The Western Cape Provincial Government has initiated formal steps that could lead to the dissolution of the Knysna municipal council. In cases of severe governmance failure, provincial authorities can step in and place a municipality under administration.

Local Government MEC Anton Bredell issued a 66 page notice to the Council on the 26th of June 2025 outlining why the municipality has failed to fulfill its executive obligations, and why intervention is justified. He plans to recommend to the Provincial Executive that the Knysna council be dissolved and an administrator appointed. Elections would need to follow within ninety days - allowing residents to reset the town politically. But, residents are divided over what will be best for the town - some say the new Mayor is turning things around and needs more time, others say, there is no hope with this council in place. Meanwhile, the town is on the verge of complete infrastructure collapse, with sewage spills into the estuary at an all time high, and a visible and terrifying deterioration since we were last there 18 months ago.



Summary:
At the heart of this political deadlock is a council deeply divided along party lines. A request by the majority in council for an extension to respond to Bredell’s notice was denied, intensifying tensions. They have been granted a fourteen day extension to respond to Bredell’s notice of intention. Civil society groups and the local business community have warned that years of mismanagement, service delivery failures, and financial instability have left Knysna in a state of collapse.

This story represents a national test case for dysfunctional municipalities. With the possibility of imminent elections if the council is dissolved and Knysna is placed under administration, this is a critical moment. Will placing Knysna under administration be a lifeline – or a last resort too long delayed?



Further information:
This developing crisis has been triggered by political infighting, and this story would examine what placing the town under administration will mean for residents, councillors and service delivery. If elections are called (they must be held within ninety days if council is dissolved) will they offer a path to recovery or risk further fragmentation? There are concerns that if there are new elections there will not be enough time for proper campaigning and there is a risk of repeating current governance dynamics if public participation is low. The new Mayor Thando Matika is by all accounts doing a better job than former ANC mayor Aubrey Tsengwa, but he has only been in that position since March. The council's response to Bredell on 18 July was that if council is dissolved they will get an interdict to stop it. Only the DA (the official opposition in Council) was in favour of Bredell's intention to dissolve council and hold fresh elections.

Script:


ERIN: Visible signs of infrastructure collapse are everywhere. Despite just over a billion rand budget, Knysna is on the brink of financial collapse. (Date February 2024)

VO 1 A town in freefall - this was the Knysna we visited eighteen months ago.

VO 2 Infrastructure collapse after years of municipal neglect…

VO 3 Council meetings that regularly descended into chaos…

NATSOUND Knsyna montage of council meeting (DATE STAMP 31 January 2024)
“Councillors, councillors, councillors, you cannot mention the ANC, the ANC cannot be quiet”

VO 4 And, it’s estuary contaminated by raw sewage.

VO 5 Our story divided opinion on who was to blame, what should happen next….and, more importantly, who could save the town..

VO 6 Now, we’re back to find out if things have improved.. or possibly… gotten worse.

FADE TO BLACK

VO 7 Knysna, known as the Jewel of the Garden Route, has the most biodiverse estuary in the country.

VO 8 But, sewage spills make their way downhill into this once pristine lagoon. The decline visible everywhere - from the main road - to the surrounding informal settlements.

LINK This water here was recently tested, revealing shocking results – extremely high levels of e.coli. Over 21 000 percent higher than what is considered to be safe.

VO 9 At the garden refuse tip at the top of Old Place suburb, overflows in the municipal drain system have not been fixed since our last visit. Ilegal dumping continues.

VO 10 In some suburbs the stench of sewage hangs in the air.

VO 11 For Wynona Morris, who has lived in Hornlee for 25 years, conditions are worse than ever.

UPSOUND Wynona Morris / Knysna Resident: That one was for six week, we have to walk through there in this shit. And they know about it. They come after three or four weeks. We live in that smell day after day.

VO 12 She’s desperate for change.

UPSOUND Wynona Morris: There should be a different council. I don’t care what they think, if they come after me. But, nuh uh, they are not good.

NATSOUND Aubrey Tsengwa: Whoever is saying that this is a coalition of corruption I want to dispute that nonsense. It’s nonsene. (DATE Stamp Feb 2024)

VO 13 The Knysna Local Municipality has been run by an ANC led coalition since August 2022, with the ANC’s Aubrey Tsengwa as mayor – until recently.

VO 14 When we interviewed him last year, he confidently claimed he could turn the town around.

UPSOUND Former Mayor Aubrey Tsengwa (From FIRST story) Clip 469 / Day 1 40:554 Yes, I’m the right person to lead the town despite these small challenges which we are facing at the municipality. And I’ve said the officials are working around the clock. (DATE this Carte Blanche FEBRUARY 2024)

VO 15 Turns out those challenges were anything but small.

VO 16 In February this year, Tsengwa was removed as mayor in a motion of no confidence and was replaced by another ANC councillor, Thando Matika.

VO 17 He’s asking residents for patience.

UPSOUND Thando Matika / Knysna Executive: They have been giving us time for the last ten years. And we keep on saying that it’s aging infrastructure. We keep on saying its financial instability. We are saying give us time, some of the administration is not even here for six months. We are dealing with it.

VO 18 At the Waste Transfer station in the centre of town, the refuse removal truck has broken down - yet again.

MASA: We were here eighteen months ago, there was just waste piling up there and there’s still waste piling up there. What’s going on there?

UPSOUND Mayor Thando Matika/ Knysna Mayor: The issue of the truck it’s unfortunate, we have set aside money to buy an extra truck so that we can assist, because if the truck is not working we are using service providers.

LINK Knysna’s story is no longer just a local scandal. It’s a national warning. What happens when leadership fails, oversight is ignored, and a town is left to rot? And in the end, who will be held accountable - if anyone?

VO 19 A string of legal battles have also contributed to the town’s decline. Two Western Cape High Court judgments found appointments made during former mayor Tsengwa’s tenure unlawful.

VO 20 But having left office under a cloud, Tsengwa is back in council. He resigned as a ward councillor earlier this year, triggering a by-election. Incredibly the ANC put him forward as their candidate. And … he won.

MASA : Surely he is to blame for a bulk of these challenges that you’re now trying to fix?

UPSOUND Mayor Matika: I think maybe all of us need to be blamed because he was not there alone, all of us were there.

MASA: If this is collective accountability, then why should the residents trust that you are going to fix it, if you were part of the problem?

UPSOUND Mayor Matika I’m saying that there’s a new mayor, I understand that we had a previous mayor, but now there is a new mayor. In this coalition we are working close with the EFF, we are working close with PA, PBI. We believe we are making some strides, they are not big strides. But as we say anything related to service delivery you start with your finance, so we have improved in terms of our finance.

VO 21 An ANC led coalition might govern in Knysna, but the Democratic Alliance runs the Western Cape. It has the power to intervene where municipalities are failing.

LINK I’m about to interview the man who holds the future of Knysna in his hands - that would be the MEC for local government in the Western Cape, Anton Bredell. Now, could this be a moment of the beginning of change for the residents of Knysna or just another chapter in a long running collapse?

VO 22 In June, Bredell informed the Knysna Municipality of his intention to intervene saying service delivery and the environment risked more damage unless “extraordinary action” is taken by the Provincial Government. He blamed protracted and ongoing systemic governance and service delivery failures.

UPSOUND Anton Bredell WCape Local Government MEC: It’s not a resource problem. It’s a management and a leadership problem. And the only way to solve that is to put them under administration, to get a team of experts there from national, from provincial and national treasury and then tackle these problems and solve them.

MASA: Why now after prolonged decline?

UPSOUND Anton Bredell: It takes a long time to build up the evidence. You will pick up from Knysna they will most probably take me to court. And then the court will make a judgment on that and say yes you can intervene or not. It’s a serious step. It’s a last resort.

VO 23 Bredell claims they’ve tried all other options.

UPSOUND Anton Bredell: Well, we tried to support them for the last six years and our support is just not enough. And it’s not a money problem. We’ve put in from the Province side over R50 million in Knysna already over the last couple of years. We’ve got a responsibility as a government to see to it that every municipality works because of the dignified life we want to give to citizens. This is not personal, this is not politically driven.

UPSOUND Mayor Thando Matika: It will not even assist the residents of Knysna to dissolve the Municipality. It’s political, its trying to bring back this municipality into dispute and into decay. Now we have to run around and try to waste time to try and respond to MEC Bredell.

VO 24 If Knysna’s council is dissolved, elections must be held within ninety days.

VO 25 Some argue this intervention should have happened as far back as November 2023 when a decomposing body was found in this municipal reservoir.

MASA: What would you say to critics who say is this really about saving Knysna or is this about politics, is this the DA’s way of stooping it to its opposition the ANC?

UPSOUND Anton Bredell: If there’s a body in your reservoir lying there for a week plus, there’s a problem, if you can’t provide water to your residents up to ten days there’s a problem. It’s a beautiful town, and its very sad that we sit here today and talk about administration.

VO 26 Desperate residents refused to stand by and watch the town collapse and formed civil society organisations, using private funds to try and fix the problems.

LINK While councillors argued, the Knysna Infrastructure Group was quietly mapping out solutions, helping to fix broken systems, proposing urgent interventions, and offering the kind of leadership that the Municipality failed to provide.

VO 27 Eugene Vermaak helped start the Knysna Infrastructure Group – an apolitical team of residents raising funds to support the municipality.

VO 28 Their work includes repairing key services, like the wastewater treatment plant.

UPSOUND Eugene Vermaak / Knysna Infrastructure Group: In September last year we raised R500,000 through local residents and we actually got ten engineers that came in for a whole week and we reestablished the whole plant.

MASA How does it make you feel as residents that you have basically taken on the role of the municipality?

UPSOUND Eugene Vermaak: We see it differently. We here to support whoever is running this municipality. There’s not a single municipality in this country’s that’s going to survive if you don’t have public private partnerships.

VO 29 Eugene doesn’t support placing the town under administration.

UPSOUND Eugene Vermaak: For the first time this council’s got permanent employees in all the director positions. The new Mayor from what we’re seen and we’ve worked with him in terms of the emergency as well, are very decisive. We could see the results.

VO 30 The emergency he’s referring to happened in May when water pumps failed. As water outages were experienced across Knysna, it turned to charitable organisations. There’ve been sporadic service delivery protests and anger continues to simmer.

VO 31 Knysna Independent Movement Councillor Susan Campbell isn’t part of the ruling coalition, but is another critic of plans to dissolve the council.

UPSOUND Susan Campbell / KIM Councillor: I don’t know if people understand if you dissolve council you get an administrator only for the time that council is dissolved which is a maximum of ninety days. Then a new council comes in.

VO 32 She says the council is far more stable than its every been, but one destabilising factor remains: former mayor Tsengwa.

UPSOUND Susan Campbell: I believe that he was a huge huge huge factor in the dysfunctionality of this municipality eighteen months ago.

VO 33 A probe by the Province into irregular staff appointments by the Knysna Council ultimately recommended Tsengwa’s removal. Campbell says THAT is what Bredell should be acting on.

UPSOUND Susan Campbell: Clearly he could not remove him from council after he resigned, but the moment he was back in council, considering this is the same term the MEC should have removed him.

VO 34 Bredell says Tsengwa’s fate is in the hands of the people who put him there in the first place.

UPSOUND Anton Bredell: If that’s the kind of leaders then they vote in, then they must understand that there will be consequences on services at the end of the day.

VO 35 Despite Tsengwa’s presence, Campbell says there are positive signs.

UPSOUND Susan Campbell: We all need the town to succeed for our tourism and for everybody who lives in it. We’ve still got huge problems, I’m not saying we don’t, but things are very much improved, ja.

VO 36 Now, another legal battle looms: the ruling coalition says it’ll fight any attempt to put Knysna under administration. The new mayor wants to be given the time to make a difference.

UPSOUND Thando Matika: It’s not like the Knysna it used to be when I was a kid. Knysna always used to be town of the year. But, we are making some strides, trying to address some of those issues.

Now we have to run around and try to waste time to try and respond to MEC Bredell. VO 24 If Knysna’s council is dissolved, elections must be held within ninety days. VO 25 Some argue this intervention should have happened as far back as November 2023 when a decomposing body was found in this municipal reservoir. MASA: What would you say to critics who say is this really about saving Knysna or is this about politics, is this the DA’s way of stooping it to its opposition the ANC? UPSOUND Anton Bredell: If there’s a body in your reservoir lying there for a week plus, there’s a problem, if you can’t provide water to your residents up to ten days there’s a problem. It’s a beautiful town, and its very sad that we sit here today and talk about administration. VO 26 Desperate residents refused to stand by and watch the town collapse and formed civil society organisations, using private funds to try and fix the problems. LINK While councillors argued, the Knysna Infrastructure Group was quietly mapping out solutions, helping to fix broken systems, proposing urgent interventions, and offering the kind of leadership that the Municipality failed to provide. VO 27 Eugene Vermaak helped start the Knysna Infrastructure Group – an apolitical team of residents raising funds to support the municipality. VO 28 Their work includes repairing key services, like the wastewater treatment plant. UPSOUND Eugene Vermaak / Knysna Infrastructure Group: In September last year we raised R500,000 through local residents and we actually got ten engineers that came in for a whole week and we reestablished the whole plant. MASA How does it make you feel as residents that you have basically taken on the role of the municipality? UPSOUND Eugene Vermaak: We see it differently. We here to support whoever is running this municipality. There’s not a single municipality in this country’s that’s going to survive if you don’t have public private partnerships. VO 29 Eugene doesn’t support placing the town under administration. UPSOUND Eugene Vermaak: For the first time this council’s got permanent employees in all the director positions. The new Mayor from what we’re seen and we’ve worked with him in terms of the emergency as well, are very decisive. We could see the results. VO 30 The emergency he’s referring to happened in May when water pumps failed. As water outages were experienced across Knysna, it turned to charitable organisations. There’ve been sporadic service delivery protests and anger continues to simmer. VO 31 Knysna Independent Movement Councillor Susan Campbell isn’t part of the ruling coalition, but is another critic of plans to dissolve the council. UPSOUND Susan Campbell / KIM Councillor: I don’t know if people understand if you dissolve council you get an administrator only for the time that council is dissolved which is a maximum of ninety days. Then a new council comes in. VO 32 She says the council is far more stable than its every been, but one destabilising factor remains: former mayor Tsengwa. UPSOUND Susan Campbell: I believe that he was a huge huge huge factor in the dysfunctionality of this municipality eighteen months ago. VO 33 A probe by the Province into irregular staff appointments by the Knysna Council ultimately recommended Tsengwa’s removal. Campbell says THAT is what Bredell should be acting on. UPSOUND Susan Campbell: Clearly he could not remove him from council after he resigned, but the moment he was back in council, considering this is the same term the MEC should have removed him. VO 34 Bredell says Tsengwa’s fate is in the hands of the people who put him there in the first place. UPSOUND Anton Bredell: If that’s the kind of leaders then they vote in, then they must understand that there will be consequences on services at the end of the day. VO 35 Despite Tsengwa’s presence, Campbell says there are positive signs. UPSOUND Susan Campbell: We all need the town to succeed for our tourism and for everybody who lives in it. We’ve still got huge problems, I’m not saying we don’t, but things are very much improved, ja. VO 36 Now, another legal battle looms: the ruling coalition says it’ll fight any attempt to put Knysna under administration. The new mayor wants to be given the time to make a difference. UPSOUND Thando Matika: It’s not like the Knysna it used to be when I was a kid. Knysna always used to be town of the year. But, we are making some strides, trying to address some of those issues.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Knysna, once the jewel of the Garden Route, is on a knife edge - steps to dissolve its council and place the town under administration have been initiated, but is it too little too late?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The Western Cape Provincial Government has initiated formal steps that could lead to the dissolution of the Knysna municipal council. In cases of severe governmance failure, provincial authorities can step in and place a municipality under administration. Local Government MEC Anton Bredell issued a 66 page notice to the Council on the 26th of June 2025 outlining why the municipality has failed to fulfill its executive obligations, and why intervention is justified. He plans to recommend to the Provincial Executive that the Knysna council be dissolved and an administrator appointed. Elections would need to follow within ninety days - allowing residents to reset the town politically. But, residents are divided over what will be best for the town - some say the new Mayor is turning things around and needs more time, others say, there is no hope with this council in place. Meanwhile, the town is on the verge of complete infrastructure collapse, with sewage spills into the estuary at an all time high, and a visible and terrifying deterioration since we were last there 18 months ago.
metadata.Summary: At the heart of this political deadlock is a council deeply divided along party lines. A request by the majority in council for an extension to respond to Bredell’s notice was denied, intensifying tensions. They have been granted a fourteen day extension to respond to Bredell’s notice of intention. Civil society groups and the local business community have warned that years of mismanagement, service delivery failures, and financial instability have left Knysna in a state of collapse. This story represents a national test case for dysfunctional municipalities. With the possibility of imminent elections if the council is dissolved and Knysna is placed under administration, this is a critical moment. Will placing Knysna under administration be a lifeline – or a last resort too long delayed?
metadata.Further information: This developing crisis has been triggered by political infighting, and this story would examine what placing the town under administration will mean for residents, councillors and service delivery. If elections are called (they must be held within ninety days if council is dissolved) will they offer a path to recovery or risk further fragmentation? There are concerns that if there are new elections there will not be enough time for proper campaigning and there is a risk of repeating current governance dynamics if public participation is low. The new Mayor Thando Matika is by all accounts doing a better job than former ANC mayor Aubrey Tsengwa, but he has only been in that position since March. The council's response to Bredell on 18 July was that if council is dissolved they will get an interdict to stop it. Only the DA (the official opposition in Council) was in favour of Bredell's intention to dissolve council and hold fresh elections.
